label: Hotel supplier requests (hotel level)
purpose: Hotel-level statistics of the requests GTE sends to hotel suppliers: each hotel asked counts once, with its outcome (OK, no results, other failure), cache use, room-rate combinations and look-to-book, by hotel, destination, customer and travel window. Data only from 2026-08-17.
grain: Hotel requests (one hotel asked in a supplier request) aggregated per request day, supplier connection, customer, credential, hotel, request type and context, availability type, interface and travel window.
use_for: supplier hotel-request outcomes (OK, KO, no results, other failures) and their rates
which hotels, cities or countries are requested from suppliers
supplier hotel requests by travel window (days before check-in)
cached hotel requests with and without availability
not_for: request-message counts, response times, time-outs or error types (Statistics History Supplier)
requests clients send to GTE (Statistics Hotel Client)

coverage.note: Recent only: data starts on 2026-08-17 and ends yesterday (2026-10-15 when read on 2026-10-16), so 2026-08 is partial and there is no earlier history. For older periods use Statistics History Supplier.

dates.label: Request date
dates.meaning: Day the hotel request was sent to the supplier. The cube's only date.

measures.name: [Total Hotel Requests]
measures.label: Supplier hotel requests
measures.definition: Hotel requests sent to suppliers: each hotel asked in a supplier request counts once. Equals OK + KO.
measures.notes: Main measure. Hotel level, so about 5 times the number of request messages in Statistics History Supplier.

measures.name: [Hotel Requests OK]
measures.label: Supplier hotel requests OK
measures.definition: Hotel requests for which the supplier returned availability.

measures.name: [Hotel Requests KO]
measures.label: Supplier hotel requests KO
measures.definition: Hotel requests that did not return availability: no results (NR) plus other failures (OTH).
measures.notes: Verified: KO = NR + OTH and OK + KO = Total.

measures.name: [Hotel Requests NR]
measures.label: Supplier hotel requests with no results
measures.definition: Hotel requests the supplier answered without availability (no results).
terms: supplier hotel requests with no results

measures.name: [Hotel Requests OTH]
measures.label: Supplier hotel requests failed (other)
measures.definition: Hotel requests that failed for a reason other than no results (supplier errors, time-outs and similar).
terms: supplier hotel requests failed with errors
measures.notes: Meaning inferred: OTH = KO minus NR. The cube has no error-type breakdown; for error kinds use Statistics History Supplier.

measures.name: [% Hotel Requests OK]
measures.label: Supplier hotel success rate
measures.definition: [Hotel Requests OK] / [Total Hotel Requests].

measures.name: [% Hotel Requests KO]
measures.label: Supplier hotel failure rate
measures.definition: [Hotel Requests KO] / [Total Hotel Requests].

measures.name: [% Hotel Requests NR]
measures.label: Supplier hotel no-results rate
measures.definition: [Hotel Requests NR] / [Total Hotel Requests].

measures.name: [% Hotel Requests OTH]
measures.label: Supplier hotel error rate
measures.definition: [Hotel Requests OTH] / [Total Hotel Requests].

measures.name: [Hotels Cached]
measures.label: Hotel requests served from cache
measures.definition: Hotel requests answered from GTE's cache instead of a live supplier call (Cached OK + Cached NR).
terms: supplier hotel requests served from cache

measures.name: [Hotels Cached Ok]
measures.label: Cached hotel requests with availability
measures.definition: Cached hotel requests that returned availability.
terms: cached supplier hotel requests with availability

measures.name: [Hotels Cached NR]
measures.label: Cached hotel requests with no results
measures.definition: Cached hotel requests that returned no availability.
terms: cached supplier hotel requests with no results

measures.name: [% Hotels Cached]
measures.label: Supplier hotel cache rate
measures.definition: [Hotels Cached] / [Total Hotel Requests].
terms: share of supplier hotel requests served from cache

measures.name: [% Hotels Cached OK]
measures.label: Cached hotel requests with availability (%)
measures.definition: [Hotels Cached Ok] / [Hotels Cached].

measures.name: [% Hotels Cached NR]
measures.label: Cached hotel requests with no results (%)
measures.definition: [Hotels Cached NR] / [Hotels Cached].

measures.name: [Combinations]
measures.label: Room-rate combinations returned
measures.definition: Room/board/rate combinations (options) suppliers returned for the hotels requested.
measures.notes: Not a request count: about 18 per hotel request. The schema's value counts are in this measure.

measures.name: [Avg Combinations]
measures.label: Average combinations per hotel request
measures.definition: [Combinations] / [Total Hotel Requests] (all hotel requests, including those without availability).
terms: average room combinations per supplier hotel request
measures.notes: Verified ratio. Per successful request it would be about 1.7 times higher.

measures.name: [L2B]
measures.label: Hotel supplier look-to-book
measures.definition: Look-to-book ratio reported by this cube: hotel requests per booking. Exact inverse of [% L2B].
measures.notes: About 4 million hotel requests per booking. Its booking count is not exposed and differs from Statistics History Supplier's, so the two L2B values are not comparable. Blank or meaningless when grouped by 'Context' or 'Request Types'.

measures.name: [% L2B]
measures.label: Hotel supplier booking conversion
measures.definition: Bookings per hotel request, the inverse of [L2B], as a fraction.

measures.name: [Avg Days Travel Window]
measures.label: Average travel window (days)
measures.definition: Meant to be the average number of days between the request and check-in.
measures.hidden_reason: broken: returns about 0 and negative values (overall 0.02, last 12 months -0.008; -0.11 inside the '3 to 7 Days' band). Use [Total Hotel Requests] by 'Travel Window'[Description] instead.

breakdowns.label: Customer payment type

breakdowns.label: Agency group

breakdowns.meaning: Kind of call sent to the supplier. Almost all hotel requests are Availability.

breakdowns.meaning: Customer channel that triggered the supplier request: XML (almost all), WEB or CLC.

rules: This is supplier-side traffic (GTE -> hotel suppliers) counted per hotel. Requests clients send to GTE are in Statistics Hotel Client; searches are in Statistics Zone.

Data exists only from 2026-08-17. For a period that starts earlier, say so and use Statistics History Supplier instead (its [Hotels Request] is the closest measure, about 8% higher in the same month because its scope is wider).
Data ends yesterday; for today use Statistics Real Time Supplier.
[Total Hotel Requests] = [Hotel Requests OK] + [Hotel Requests KO], and KO = NR + OTH. The % measures are shares of [Total Hotel Requests]; the cached % measures are shares of [Hotels Cached].
Only the count measures add up. Percentages, averages, [L2B] and [% L2B] must never be summed or averaged across rows, days or suppliers.

[L2B] / [% L2B] are only meaningful by date, supplier, customer or hotel attributes; grouped by 'Context' or 'Request Types' they are blank or meaningless. Do not compare them with Statistics History Supplier's L2B (different basis).
[Avg Days Travel Window] is broken and hidden: answer lead-time questions with [Total Hotel Requests] by 'Travel Window'[Description].

Suppliers are identified by their connection code 'Suppliers'[Supplier Code] (always with 'Suppliers'[Supplier Code.UniqueName]); 'Suppliers'[Supplier] is the connection's name. The Bookings cube names suppliers differently: joining to Bookings is by name only and may not match well, so say so whenever you combine them.
'Hotels'[Hotel] has 3.4 million values and 'Hotels'[City] 79 thousand: always filter them or take a top N. Use 'Hotels'[JP Code] to follow one hotel across suppliers.
Use the cube's measures only; never SUM a column.

review.question: Does "failed supplier hotel requests" mean all KO (no results + other failures) or only OTH (errors)?
review.why: KO is the cube's own opposite of OK; 'supplier hotel error rate' is kept for OTH and 'no-results rate' for NR, so each word has one measure.

review.question: For supplier look-to-book in periods both cubes cover (from 2026-08-17), which cube answers: Statistics History Supplier (requests per booking) or this cube (hotel requests per booking)?
review.why: History has a year of data and a request-level basis; the two cubes count bookings differently (about 1.5 million vs 4 million per booking in September), so one definition must be used everywhere.

review.question: [Avg Days Travel Window] returns about 0 and negative values. Keep it hidden until the cube is fixed?
review.why: Its values contradict the travel-window bands (nearly half of the hotel requests are 1 to 6 months ahead); showing it would give wrong lead times.
